rv.q: The bag of make-believe faeces that splashes onto the stage towards the end of the evening turns out to be an all too apt metaphor for what we have had to endure.
Under director Walter Meierjohann’s guidance, the cast and creative team have generated an absurdist dynamic, which constantly surprises, tickles and unsettles.

Its ability to surprise and delight through miraculous writing and ingenious direction and the sensational performances from actors at the top of their game barely scratch the surface as to what makes this production so utterly exceptional.
We came to see Whishaw, who's always reliably brilliant on a stage as he is here, but left bowled over by an age-defying performance from the formidable Kathryn Hunter.
'Eurotrash' is a devilishly funny meditation on greed, guilt and reckoning.
On those terms it's satisfying because the stars absolutely deliver like you'd hope they would

cn.t: Critics embrace Eurotrash as a wildly absurdist delight, with Ben Whishaw and Kathryn Hunter delivering standout performances. A surprising, unsettling, and frequently hilarious adaptation that ranks among the Young Vic's best.
